definitions.explanation: One's spouse's father, or a stepfather. The 義理 prefix indicates a family relationship by marriage rather than blood.

examples.japanese: {義理|ぎり}の{父|ちち}に{挨拶|あいさつ}した。
{義理|ぎり}の{父|ちち}とは{仲|なか}が{良|よ}い。
examples.english: I get along well with my father-in-law.

examples.japanese: {結婚|けっこん}して{初|はじ}めて{義理|ぎり}の{父|ちち}の{家|いえ}を{訪|たず}ねた{時|とき}は、とても{緊張|きんちょう}した。
examples.english: I was very nervous when I visited my father-in-law's house for the first time after getting married.

notes:
USAGE:
The {義理|ぎり}の〜 pattern creates in-law family terms: {義理|ぎり}の{父|ちち} (father-in-law), {義理|ぎり}の{母|はは} (mother-in-law), {義理|ぎり}の{兄弟|きょうだい} (brother/sister-in-law). When speaking about one's own father-in-law to others, use {義理|ぎり}の{父|ちち}. When addressing him directly, use お{義父|とう}さん.

NOTE: {義理|ぎり} here indicates a relationship by marriage, not by blood.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {義理|ぎり}の{父|ちち}に{会|あ}う (to meet one's father-in-law)
- {義理|ぎり}の{両親|りょうしん} (parents-in-law)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {義父|ぎふ}: father-in-law — formal/written equivalent
- お{義父|とう}さん: father-in-law — polite address form
- {舅|しゅうと}: father-in-law — traditional term, also read しゅうとめ for mother-in-law
